message.reasoning_content:
The contract requires bitwise determinism across calls. Atomic float add order is nondeterministic. But with all values on dequant grid, sums might be exact... 65536 elements, magnitudes up to ~1, each block sum of 1024 elements exact? Each element k*2^-7, sum of 1024 such = k_total*2^-7, up to 127*1024 = ~130048, still exactly representable in fp32 (integers up to 2^24). So block partials are exact. Then atomic adds of exact integer multiples of 2^-7 up to total 65536*127*2^-7 ≈ 65024, still exact in fp32. So rounding may be exact regardless of order — nondeterminism may not matter. Need probe.

Claim: atomic ordering makes results nondeterministic. Probe: run many times, check bitwise equality on representative inputs (dequant grid). Also test adversarial: all max values, mixed signs (cancellation not an issue since exact multiples). All sums exact → bitwise identical. So maybe trust.

But wait — tl.sum within block: order fixed within block? Tree reduction exact for these values anyway. Partial sum is exact multiple of 2^-7, magnitude ≤ 127*1024=130048 < 2^24*2^-7? fp32 can represent integer multiples of 2^-7 up to 2^17 magnitude... 2^24 * 2^-7 = 2^17 = 131072. Block sum max 130048 < 131072, exact. Total sum max 127*65536/128 = 65024 < 131072, exact. All additions exact regardless of order. So deterministic.

Record claim and probe.
